mechanism_narrative: A low federal funds rate (FEDFUNDS) indicates accommodative monetary policy, reducing discount rates for equity valuation and producing positive S&P 500 forward returns over 20 trading days. The effect is continuous: lower FEDFUNDS values correlate with higher returns.
failure_condition: Pearson correlation between FEDFUNDS and 20-day returns is not negative (i.e., > -0.1) over any 3-year rolling window, or Rank IC < 0.03.

mechanism_narrative: Federal funds rate (FEDFUNDS) exceeding 5.0% signals monetary tightening, increasing discount rates and compressing equity valuations, leading to negative S&P 500 forward returns over 20 trading days.
failure_condition: In FEDFUNDS > 5.0 periods, 20-day returns are not negative in > 60% of cases, or Rank IC < 0.03 over 3-year windows.

mechanism_narrative: Simultaneous housing starts (HOUST) and retail sales (RSAFS) above 12-month moving averages indicate strong consumer demand, supporting earnings growth and driving positive S&P 500 forward returns over 20 trading days.
failure_condition: Condition (HOUST and RSAFS > 12mo_MA) produces positive 20-day returns in ≤ 60% of cases, or interaction Rank IC < 0.03.

mechanism_narrative: In late-cycle expansion, UNRATE above 5.0% signals labor market tightness, prompting central bank tightening and negative S&P 500 forward returns over 5 trading days.
failure_condition: In late-cycle expansion, UNRATE > 5.0 periods produce negative 5-day returns in ≤ 60% of cases, or Rank IC < 0.03.

mechanism_narrative: Housing starts (HOUST) exceeding 1500 thousand units indicates robust housing market strength, supporting consumer spending and driving positive S&P 500 forward returns over 60 trading days.
failure_condition: HOUST > 1500 periods produce positive 60-day returns in ≤ 60% of cases, or Rank IC < 0.03.

mechanism_narrative: Declining industrial production (INDPRO < 110) combined with rising CPI (CPIAUCSL > 205) indicates supply shock dynamics, prompting central bank intervention and positive S&P 500 forward returns over 20 trading days.
failure_condition: Condition (INDPRO<110 and CPIAUCSL>205) produces positive 20-day returns in ≤ 60% of cases, or interaction Rank IC < 0.03.

mechanism_narrative: High employment levels (PAYEMS) indicate strong labor market conditions supporting consumer spending and corporate earnings growth, producing positive S&P 500 forward returns over 20 trading days. The effect is continuous: higher PAYEMS values correlate with higher returns.
failure_condition: Pearson correlation between PAYEMS and 20-day returns is not positive (i.e., < 0.1) over any 3-year rolling window, or Rank IC < 0.03.

mechanism_narrative: Consumer price inflation (CPIAUCSL) exceeding 205.0 indicates accelerating inflation, prompting central bank tightening and negative S&P 500 forward returns over 20 trading days.
failure_condition: In CPIAUCSL > 205.0 periods, 20-day returns are not negative in > 60% of cases, or Rank IC < 0.03 over 3-year windows.
